job_description_info.job_description:
# Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform

**Company:** Halden Pay (fictional name; cross-border business payments)
**Location:** Lisbon, Portugal (hybrid, 3 days per week in the office)
**Team:** Data Platform

## The role

Halden Pay is growing quickly, and data sits at the centre of that plan. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join the Data Platform team. The team builds and runs the shared data platform that analysts, data scientists and product teams rely on, with a focus on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines.

## Responsibilities

- Own the design, build and day-to-day running of the company's central data platform
- Evaluate and introduce new open-source tools where they bring a clear benefit
- Work with data scientists, analytics engineers and BI colleagues to turn their needs into platform features
- Define and enforce data quality standards, governance rules and access policies

## Tech stack

- Cloud: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE)
- Orchestration and transformation: Airflow, dbt
- Engineering: Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, Git

## Requirements

- Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
- Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
- Strong data modelling skills (dimensional modelling; graph modelling is a plus)
- Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
- Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
- Good professional English; Portuguese is a plus

If you meet most but not all of the points above, you are still welcome to apply.

## Benefits

- Base salary plus annual bonus
- Training and certification budget
- Support for open-source contributions
- Hybrid work from a central Lisbon office

Senior Data Engineer
Rijeka, Croatia (open to remote, EU time zones) | lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example

Data engineer with 9 years of experience building batch and streaming data platforms for e-commerce and payments. I like boring, well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts and warehouses that analysts actually trust.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. With nine years of experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud warehouses, I have focused on creating reliable, reusable systems that make trusted data accessible to analytics and product teams. Halden Pay’s emphasis on a shared platform and reusable frameworks is a strong match for my work building reusable ingestion, transformation, data-quality, and platform tooling.

In my current role, I own ingestion and orchestration across a production platform with around 140 Airflow DAGs and Snowflake. I migrated warehouse transformations to more than 420 tested dbt models and introduced incremental models and slim CI, reducing nightly build time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. This included optimising large-scale warehouse workloads through incremental models and state:modified CI. I have also defined and enforced JSON Schema data contracts with CI checks, helping establish repeatable data-quality standards between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents, and built a Kafka shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events a day. These projects reflect my hands-on experience with Python, SQL, data modelling, CI/CD and operating data systems at scale. I also designed a Redshift warehouse using a dimensional star schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams.

My cloud experience includes AWS, including EMR, S3 and Glue, alongside Snowflake and Redshift. I have also contributed two merged pull requests to an open-source Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests. Across these experiences, I have aimed to improve reliability and simplify platform work, while mentoring colleagues and working across teams—an approach that aligns with Halden Pay’s values of Ownership, Together and Pace.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my data-platform experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional cover letter with a clear connection to the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. It uses relevant evidence rather than generic claims, including 140 Airflow DAGs, 420+ dbt models, measurable build-time improvement, 30 million daily Kafka events, Redshift dimensional modelling, AWS, and open-source contributions. The tone is confident and appropriately concise. The main opportunity is to make a few job-critical capabilities more explicit and to improve the readability of the dense second paragraph.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly because it uses standard headings-free letter structure, conventional paragraphs, and relevant keywords including data platforms, cloud warehouses, Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, Redshift, data modelling, CI/CD, AWS, EMR, S3, Glue, and open source. AI screening probability is high for the core role because the letter contains quantified evidence and closely matches the job terminology. It could perform slightly better by explicitly using the phrases "production data platform," "query optimisation," "dimensional modelling," "data quality standards," and "reusable frameworks." The long second paragraph contains several separate achievements and would be easier for both human and AI reviewers to process if split into two paragraphs or tightened.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the role. It demonstrates experience designing, building, and operating a production data platform at scale; Airflow and dbt; Python and SQL; Snowflake and Redshift; dimensional modelling; AWS as a comparable cloud environment; data quality; CI/CD; platform reliability; mentoring; and open-source practices. The reference to Halden Pay's values—Ownership, Together and Pace—is relevant and supported by the candidate's mentoring, cross-team data contracts, and reliability work. The candidate's material does not show Google Cloud specifically, graph modelling, or Portuguese. These are genuine profile gaps rather than document defects and should not be presented as deficiencies in the letter.

This is supported by the documented Python, SQL, incremental dbt models, warehouse build-time reduction, and Redshift star-schema experience.
